content.title: Could Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 Get Pushed to 2027 if It Doesn't Make It Before GTA 6?
content.text: During the big Forza Horizon 6 gameplay reveal, Playground Games studio confirmed that while it’s coming to Xbox Series X|S and PC on May 19, it won’t arrive on PlayStation 5 systems at launch. The PS5 versions are bound for “later in 2026.” It goes without saying that any talk about Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 and PS5 Pro slipping from 2026 to 2027 is purely speculative. However, that doesn’t make the possibility any less true. It could happen because of GTA VI, and not just to FH6, but to a bunch of other titles planned for this fall, including Playgrounds’ other big AAA game, Fable. But before getting all doom and gloom about it, Grand Theft Auto VI actually releasing on November 19 this year would certainly be quite a sight to behold. It already went through two delays, which didn't come cheap for Take-Two Interactive Software, Rockstar Games’ parent company. In November 2025, when IGN asked the T2 CEO, Strauss Zelnick, about a possible third slip, he said he was quite sure that won't happen. The second delay, from May 26 to November 19, came after the Rockstar developers decided they needed more time for polishing. According to Strauss, they wanted to “Make sure that it was spectacular and that time has been well-spent.”Photo: Xbox More poignantly, Strauss said, “When our competitors go to market before something was ready, bad things happen. That said, I’m highly confident on the new date.” It’s hard to argue that GTA 6 will get pushed back a third time to 2027. So, with that in mind, let’s pretend that it’s indeed arriving on time. For better or worse, that within itself poses an existential threat, if you will, to all the other games that might have normally been released near the GTA 6 timeline. If you take a look around the industry, at the moment, there are very few AAA publishers and developers, if any, who openly put a pin on an October, November, or even December launch date on their upcoming games. We still don’t know when PlayStation’s Wolverine is due, which is one of the most-anticipated hits of this year. It would be unfortunate if it came out anywhere near Grand Theft Auto VI. It’s one of the few that might have a fighting chance, but a September or early October window would make more sense. The only AAA title of renown that we know about (at the time of writing) set for release near GTA 6 is Phantom Blade 0. Spoiler alert, I use the term “near” loosely, as it’s due on September 9, with more than enough space between them. Some might even call that a pretty safe distance. Photo: Xbox Pulling a 180 to Playground Games, the studio is not only working on FH6, but also on another overly ambitious title, Fable, an open-world fairytale RPG, which is scheduled for this fall. One might assume that the lack of an exact release date or even a specific month might have something to do with Grand Theft Auto VI as well. The Forza Horizon 6 team is still hard at work at bringing the game to Xbox Series X|S and PC. As we know from late last year, it’s all hands-on deck, especially since the Turn 10 Studios developers have stopped making new content for Forza Motorsport to work on Horizon 6. “As our team shifts its focus toward delivering the best possible experience with Forza Horizon 6 in 2026, we do not plan to introduce new cars, tracks, features, or regular bug fixes for Forza Motorsport,” they wrote in the official Forza blog post on December 16, 2025. So, Playground Games has its hands full with FH6 and Fable, while Turn 10 Studios is also busy with Horizon 6. Suffice it to say that’s not a short order. These are two extremely ambitions games we’re talking about, not your run of the mill experience. I brought all of that up to help paint as complete a picture as possible of major publishers and developers who are actively trying to avoid GTA 6 in order to give their games the best possible chance. Photo: Xbox Now that we know how much Playground Games has on its plate, it stands to reason to look at everything through a pragmatic lens. Meaning that if the Forza Horizon 6 PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 5 Pro versions aren’t ready until mid-October at the latest, it might just be that Sony fans won’t get to play it until January 2027. Still, let’s hope for the best and expect a PS5 version at some point during late summer or late September even. However, let’s take into account that FH6 and Fable mustn’t overlap so as not compete with each other. That happened to Titanfall 2 and Battlefield 1 in 2016, and we haven’t heard anything about another Titanfall since then. In the meantime, Xbox Series X|S and PC users can expect the Forza Horizon 6 Standard Edition at $70, while the Premium Edition costs a whopping $120. For that price, you get to play it four days early, along with a VIP Membership, Welcome Pack, Time Attack Car Pack, and Car Pass with 30 cars, delivered one per week. You also get the Italian Passion Car Pack and two Premium Expansions post-launch. Lastly, it’s out on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass, so you can bet dollars to donuts that millions of people will be playing FH6 on day one. I wouldn’t be surprised to see an official social media post saying that over 10 million people have played Horizon 6 in the first week at launch. Liked the article?
